title: Reset keyboard layout before suspend lock
head: 3f745c0e8f6f
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new synchronous Hyprland IPC call bypasses the inhibitor deadline
leads.consequence: A slow Hyprland IPC request uses the remaining delay budget before the security-status poll. With a 1000ms budget and a stub configured to answer secure on the next status query but taking 2s to answer switchxkblayout, this script never reached that status query: it reported failure after ~2010ms and warned of an insecure lock despite the stub's configured secure state. If the shell has not secured yet, the budget can expire before another request/status check and logind may suspend regardless of the inhibitor. The already issued request may nevertheless finish later.
leads.triage: already_in_opus; Corroborates Opus F1 (unbounded hyprctl on inhibitor path). Published.

leads.summary: A failed layout switch is silently treated as successful locking
leads.consequence: If the compositor instance socket is absent/stale or switchxkblayout temporarily fails, the exit code and diagnostic are discarded. The lock can still become secure and sleep-lock exits 0, so the original non-Latin layout persists into the lock screen; neither the poll nor the next loop retries the reset, and the next suspend is the only automatic retry. This does not imply the screen is unlocked, only that the password-layout fix did not apply.
leads.triage: dropped; Ignored hyprctl failure matches manual lock path and Opus's confirmed fail-fast behaviour; not a defect worth publishing.

leads.summary: Index 0 does not guarantee a Latin layout for user overrides
leads.consequence: On a user-defined input config with a non-Latin first layout, e.g. ru,us, selecting index 0 leaves the lock-screen password input in that layout. Stock vconsole-derived layouts explicitly prepend us for known non-Latin defaults, but the separate user input override can reorder layouts; the existing manual lock reset has the same precondition, so this is a limit of the claimed fix, not a regression unique to suspend. A user with a Latin password must select a Latin layout manually or change the config.
leads.triage: already_in_opus; Matches Opus F4 (index 0 not always Latin). Published as comment-wording note.

leads.summary: The sleep-lock fixture does not assert the new reset at all
leads.consequence: All 19 existing sleep-lock assertions passed even after removing exactly the new switchxkblayout command from an explicitly disposable copy; the tests do not stub hyprctl themselves or record its order, success or deadline usage. A regression that reintroduces the non-Latin suspend password problem would remain green. Add a mock hyprctl call log and assert an index-0 reset between the first request and clamshell/status, plus a stall/failure case.
leads.triage: already_in_opus; Merged with Opus F3 (no assertion of the new call). Published as Optional test improvement.

leads.summary: The sleep-monitor integration fixture replaces the modified helper wholesale
leads.consequence: The test injects an echo-only omarchy-system-sleep-lock at OMARCHY_PATH instead of the script modified by this PR, so an event and a 'locked' log cannot establish that a keyboard layout was reset or that hyprctl reached the session. Its current four assertions pass but provide no new integration coverage. An end-to-end fixture should call the real helper with private mocks and confirm the hyprctl arguments and bounded timing.
leads.triage: dropped; sleep-monitor fixture substitution is pre-existing test design, low value for this PR.

leads.summary: A related open PR proposes restoring the pre-suspend non-Latin layout on resume, which would undo this fix before unlock if made runnable
leads.consequence: PR #13005 proposes saving active index 1 immediately before this PR's reset and restoring it on PrepareForSleep=false, while the session remains locked; if that helper is repaired and this ordering merges unchanged, the resumed password field again receives index 1. This is only a conditional integration risk: as posted, #13005's added helper has malformed shell syntax (merged-13005/bin/omarchy-hyprland-keyboard-layout:39-60), so its restore cannot currently be counted as executing. Coordinate their ordering, e.g. restore only after unlock rather than while password input is needed.
leads.triage: confirmed_published; Coordinator verified #13005 diff (save before sleep-lock, restore on PrepareForSleep false); Opus follow-up (followup-13005.md, review-3 run) confirmed intent conflict and that posted helper fails bash -n at line 42. Published as related-PR note.

limits: No isolated compositor session was allocated; source and sandbox stubs cannot visually verify already-visible Quickshell password input after a real suspend. A disposable VM/nested compositor with two layouts and a real sleep/wake cycle would settle it. The current syntax error in separate PR #13005 prevents confirming that PR's proposed runtime interaction as posted.

flags.claim: the new call is the only step on this path without a time bound
flags.why: Two problems with 'only ... without a time bound'. (1) It contradicts the draft's own line 11: hyprctl does have a bound, its own 5 s socket receive timeout (hyprctl/src/main.cpp:209-213; measured 5285 ms in probe:stalled, review-1). What it lacks is a script-level timeout tied to the budget. (2) The script has one more step with no script-level timeout: omarchy-notification-send in report_unsecured (head bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock:100-102), a busctl D-Bus call (bin/omarchy-notification-send:195-210). That step only runs after the deadline, on the failure path.
flags.disposition: real_error_fixed; 'only step before the deadline without a script-level timeout'

flags.claim: with the shipped 15 s window, suspend is held about 5 s longer while Hyprland is stalled
flags.why: A qualifier was lost. The extra hold equals the stall's length, up to about 5 s (hyprctl's receive timeout). In the review-1 scenario where the socket answered after 2 s, head held for 1999 ms against base's 15 ms. The table measures a socket that never answers (5467 ms against 418 ms).
flags.disposition: real_error_fixed; 'for as long as Hyprland does not answer, up to about 5 s longer'

flags.claim: The reset is not lost: hyprctl writes the request before waiting for the reply ...
flags.why: This holds in an ordinary stall, where the connection is queued and the request is written right after connect (main.cpp:234-253; review-1 probe:delayed-bounded, where the server logged the request about 2 s after the client was killed). It fails when Hyprland's accept queue is already full (listen backlog 10, HyprCtl.cpp:2341). In that case hyprctl blocks inside connect() (review-2: the 12th client and the probe hung until timeout killed them at 20 s and 12003 ms). A 0.4 s timeout would kill it before it writes, so the reset would be lost. That edge is unlikely, so the fix is only one word.

flags.claim: with a stub that sleeps 10 s, head exits 1 after 10.0 s and the bounded line exits 0 in 413 ms
flags.why: A qualifier was lost. That candidate run passed an explicit 4000 ms budget (fixture/run.sh candidate_run: "$script" 4000). Head exits 1 because a 10 s stall exceeds a 4 s budget. With the 12 s cap, head would still poll after the stall and exit 0. The timings themselves are correct: candidate:head exit 1 after 10011 ms, candidate:patched exit 0 after 413 ms.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the gap is real, and source reading shows the change fixes it in the normal case. Menu Suspend and Hibernate run `systemctl suspend`/`systemctl hibernate` directly (`default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc:38-39`), so only `omarchy-system-sleep-lock` runs on that path, and it had no layout reset. In Hyprland v0.56.2 source, `switchxkblayout all 0` moves every keyboard to its first layout and sends that group to the focused lock surface, or to the surface when it gains focus later. Against a healthy socket the call adds about 4 ms. With no Hyprland or a bad instance signature it fails fast and the lock flow continues. The call reaches the same Hyprland instance the script already uses for `sync_clamshell`.

One suggested change: the new call is the only step before the deadline without a script-level timeout.

### The layout reset can hold the suspend inhibitor for about 5 s

`omarchy-system-sleep-lock` is written so that every step fits inside logind's delay-inhibitor budget (header comment at lines 7-10). `sync_clamshell` caps its Hyprland call at 0.4 s because "lid transitions can temporarily stall Hyprland IPC". The new `hyprctl switchxkblayout all 0` at line 115 has no script-level timeout. Hyprland answers IPC on its main event loop, so when the compositor is stalled, `hyprctl` waits for its own 5 s socket receive timeout (`hyprctl/src/main.cpp:209-213`). The call runs before the first lock status poll, so the poll and any lock re-request wait for it.

Sandboxed runs with the real `hyprctl` binary against a fake Hyprland socket that never answers, and stubbed `omarchy-shell`, `busctl` and clamshell helpers:

```text
logind window  shell behaviour        base                      head
15 s (shipped) lock lands at once     exit 0 after 0.4 s        exit 0 after ~5.5 s
5 s (default)  lock lands at once     exit 0 after 0.4 s        exit 1 after 5.9 s, false "Screen did not lock before suspend" alert
5 s (default)  first request lost     re-requests, locked, 0.5 s exit 1 after 5.5 s, one request, never locked
```

**Impact:** with the shipped 15 s window, suspend is held for as long as Hyprland does not answer, up to about 5 s longer. With logind's 5 s default (the shipped drop-in not yet loaded), the whole budget goes to `hyprctl`: a lock that landed is reported as failed, and a lost first lock request is never retried, so the machine suspends unlocked where base would have locked. How often Hyprland stalls at `PrepareForSleep` was not measured.

**Suggested change:** bound it like `sync_clamshell`:

```bash
timeout --kill-after=0.1s 0.4s hyprctl switchxkblayout all 0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
```

In a labelled diagnostic copy with this line, every scenario above exited 0 within 0.93 s. The reset is normally not lost: `hyprctl` writes the request before waiting for the reply, and Hyprland runs the command before replying, so a socket that started answering 2 s later still received it.

**Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/sleep-lock-test.sh` does not stub `hyprctl`, so at head each run makes 7 real `switchxkblayout all 0` calls, which reset the layout of a developer running `./test/shell` inside Hyprland. Nothing asserts the new call. A `hyprctl` stub in `setup_scenario`, plus a stalled-`hyprctl` case modelled on "sleep lock bounds a stalled clamshell sync", would cover both: with a stub that sleeps 10 s and a 4000 ms budget, head exits 1 after 10.0 s and the bounded line exits 0 in 413 ms.

**Related open PRs:**
- #13156 fixes the same gap from `shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml` with a nonblocking `Process`, and also covers the `omarchy-restart-shell` relock and stranded-lock recovery. The two do not conflict textually; merging both would repeat the reset, which is redundant but harmless.
- #13005 is written to save the active layout before `omarchy-system-sleep-lock` runs and restore it as soon as `PrepareForSleep` signals resume, while the session is still locked. If that works as intended, the restore puts the pre-suspend (for example non-Latin) layout back on the lock screen and undoes this reset. As currently posted, #13005's new `omarchy-hyprland-keyboard-layout` helper does not parse (`bash -n` fails at line 42), so today the conflict is one of intent rather than behaviour. Worth coordinating which behaviour is wanted, for example restoring the saved layout only after unlock.

**Comment wording:** "the lock screen always receives Latin password input" holds only when the first configured layout is Latin, which Omarchy's default `input.lua` arranges for non-Latin console layouts but a hand-written `ru,us` does not.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head 3f745c0 against merge-base d201fb9. Source review of the script, the manual lock path, Hyprland v0.56.2 (`hyprctl` and IPC handling) and Qt's Wayland keyboard handling. Command-only sandbox runs of the script at base, head and a patched copy, with synthetic Hyprland sockets and stubs. `sleep-lock`, `sleep-monitor`, `keyboard-layout` and `systemd` shell tests pass at base and head. The password-field effect is from source reading, not observed in a live session. Stall frequency and duration during real suspends were not measured. #13156 was read as a diff only; #13005 was read as a diff, and its posted helper was parse-checked and run in the sandbox.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
